form.label: CVE encyclopaedia
form.description: Look up any vulnerability the feed carries, and see where it sits in this fleet. Entirely offline.

div.b: Nothing on this page is fetched from the internet.
div.span: It is read from the bundle you imported, so it says what that bundle knew when it was built and nothing more. A CVE that returns nothing is one the feed has never carried, which is not the same as one that is harmless. Coverage lists which sources the bundle actually holds.

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | eval v = if(isnull(cvss_score), "not scored", tostring(round(cvss_score,1))) | fields v
| `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | eval v = if(isnull(epss), "unscored", tostring(round(epss*100,1)) . "%") | fields v
| `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | eval v = if(kev_added != "", "YES", "not listed") | fields v
| inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" AND status="open" | stats dc(hostname) AS v | where "$cve_tok$" != ""

single.option: hosts reporting it open; zero is not "unaffected"

div.span: The four figures above, and everything below, describe one vulnerability. They stay empty until you name one: type an id in CVE id, pick a row from the search results further down, or click any CVE id anywhere else in this app. Empty here means no CVE has been chosen, not that a CVE was found to be harmless.

panel.title: What the feed says this CVE is

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | lookup riskability_cvedetail_lookup cve_id OUTPUT products AS rk_products, description AS rk_desc, assigner AS rk_assigner, published AS rk_pub | eval Product = case(coalesce(rk_products,"") != "", replace(rk_products, " ", ", "), kev_name != "", kev_name, 1=1, "The feed does not name a product. Distribution advisories describe packaging, not products; a product name needs the CVE Program source in the bundle, or a CISA KEV listing.") | eval Description = case(coalesce(rk_desc,"") != "", rk_desc, kev_description != "", kev_description, best_title != "", best_title, 1=1, "No advisory in this bundle carries a description for this CVE.") | eval "Also known as" = if(coalesce(kev_title,"") != "", kev_title, "") | eval "What CISA requires" = if(coalesce(kev_action,"") != "", kev_action, "") | eval "Ransomware campaigns" = if(coalesce(kev_ransomware,"") != "", kev_ransomware, "") | eval Published = trim(coalesce(rk_assigner,"") . " " . coalesce(rk_pub, published)) | eval CVE = cve_id | eval "Exploitation percentile" = if(isnotnull(epss_percentile), "more likely to be exploited than " . round(epss_percentile*100, 0) . "% of all scored CVEs", "") | table CVE, Product, Description, "Also known as", "Ransomware campaigns", "Exploitation percentile", Published | transpose 7 column_name="rk_label" | rename rk_label AS "About", "row 1" AS "What the feed wrote" | where 'What the feed wrote' != ""

viz.option: Pick a vulnerability from the list above, or click any CVE id anywhere in this app. If you have named one and this is still empty, the bundle was built without the CVE Program source and carries no description for it.

div.span: Each line falls back in turn. The description prefers the CVE Program's own record, then CISA's wording if it is a known exploited vulnerability, then the longest advisory text in the bundle. That last fallback matters: distribution advisories often carry no prose at all, and taking the longest of the several advisories describing one CVE recovers a description for 640,830 of the 641,374 the feed knows about. The product name has no such fallback, because only the CVE Program and CISA ever state one.

panel.title: What CISA says, and by when

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | where kev_added != "" | eval "Added to the catalogue" = kev_added | eval "Remediate by" = if(kev_due != "", kev_due, "no date given") | eval "Used in ransomware" = if(kev_ransomware != "", kev_ransomware, "not stated") | eval "CISA calls it" = if(kev_title != "", kev_title, "") | eval "What CISA requires" = if(kev_action != "", kev_action, "The catalogue entry in this bundle carries no required action. Bundles built before this app kept those fields hold only the dates.") | table "Added to the catalogue", "Remediate by", "Used in ransomware", "CISA calls it", "What CISA requires" | transpose 5 column_name="rk_label" | rename rk_label AS "About", "row 1" AS "What CISA wrote" | where 'What CISA wrote' != ""

viz.option: Not in the CISA KEV catalogue, or no CVE is selected. Absence from the catalogue is not evidence that a vulnerability is unexploited; it means CISA has not observed and published exploitation of it.

div.span: The catalogue is the one source here that reports observation rather than modelling: an entry means exploitation was seen in the wild, not predicted. Remediate by is CISA's deadline for US federal agencies. It carries no legal weight elsewhere, and is still the most defensible date to argue a change window against.

panel.title: What an attacker needs, from the CVSS vector

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | `riskability_cvss_english` | table Vector, Reach, Complexity, Privileges, "User interaction", Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability

viz.option: No CVSS vector for this CVE in the feed.

div.span: The vector spelled out, nothing more. It describes the vulnerability as published, not this fleet. Whether your copy answers a network address is a different question, and the Exposure page answers it.

panel.title: Weakness class, and the techniques mapped to it

search.query: | `riskability_cve_facts($cve_tok$)` | fields cwes | mvexpand cwes | rename cwes AS cwe | where cwe != "" | lookup riskability_attack_lookup cwe OUTPUT technique, technique_name, tactics, via_capec | eval Technique = if(isnull(technique), "no ATT&CK mapping in this bundle", technique . " " . technique_name) | eval Tactics = mvjoin(tactics, ", ") | eval Route = if(via_capec="1", "via CAPEC", "direct") | stats values(Technique) AS Technique, values(Tactics) AS Tactics, values(Route) AS Route BY cwe | rename cwe AS CWE

viz.option: No weakness class recorded for this CVE. About a third of advisories carry no CWE, and the technique mapping needs the MITRE source in the bundle.

panel.title: Find a vulnerability by product or phrase

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_cvedetail_lookup | search products="*$q_tok$*" OR description="*$q_tok$*" OR cve_id="*$q_tok$*" | head 200 | eval Product = mvindex(split(products, " "), 0) | lookup riskability_advisories_lookup cve_id OUTPUT severity, cvss_score, epss, kev_added | eval Severity = coalesce(severity, ""), CVSS = coalesce(cvss_score, ""), "EPSS %" = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss*100, 1), null()), KEV = if(coalesce(kev_added, "")!="", "yes", "") | table cve_id, Product, Severity, CVSS, "EPSS %", KEV | rename cve_id AS CVE | sort 200 - CVSS

viz.option: Type a product, a vendor or a phrase in the search box at the top. "openssl", "Red Hat", "buffer overflow". This searches the CVE Program product names and description text, so it finds vulnerabilities by what they are rather than by what your distribution happened to call the package. It needs a bundle built with the CVE Program source; without one, use the CVE box instead.

div.span: Click any row to load it above. This searches the feed, not this fleet, which is the point: an encyclopaedia has to be able to tell you about something you do not run. Capped at 200, worst CVSS first.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_findings_state_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | eval rk_key = if(match(coalesce(scope_id, ""), "^container:"), "container:" . substr(replace(scope_id, "^container:", ""), 1, 12), package) | lookup riskability_reach_lookup hostname, rk_key OUTPUT reach_class | eval Reach = coalesce(reach_class, "not assessed") | eval Accepted = if(accepted="1", "yes", "") | table hostname, package, last_version, fixed_version, scope, scope_id, confidence, Reach, status, Accepted, first_seen | rename hostname AS Host, package AS Package, last_version AS Installed, fixed_version AS "Fixed in", scope AS Scope, scope_id AS Root, confidence AS Confidence, status AS Status, first_seen AS "First seen" | sort 0 Host, Package

viz.option: Nothing in this fleet matches this CVE. That means no host reports an affected package at an affected version. It does not mean immunity: Coverage lists what the feed cannot assess at all.

panel.title: Every version that fixes this, across distributions

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_ranges_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | where fixed != "" | eval rk_eco = replace(ecosystem, "[|]", "_") | eval rk_pkg = replace(ecosystem . " " . package, "[|]", "_") | eval rk_fix = replace(package . " " . fixed . if(distro="", "", " (" . distro . ")"), "[|]", "_") | eval rk_hops = mvappend(rk_eco . "|eco|" . rk_pkg . "|pkg", rk_pkg . "|pkg|" . rk_fix . "|fix") | mvexpand rk_hops | eval rk_p = split(rk_hops, "|") | eval source = mvindex(rk_p, 0), source_kind = mvindex(rk_p, 1), target = mvindex(rk_p, 2), target_kind = mvindex(rk_p, 3) | stats count AS cves BY source, source_kind, target, target_kind | sort 200 - cves | fields source, source_kind, target, target_kind, cves

viz.option: No fixed version for this CVE in the bundle. That is common and is not an error: an advisory that names no fix has none published, so there is no upgrade to point at. Check the affected ranges below for whether a later version is merely "last affected".

div.span: One vulnerability, every packaging of it. Read left to right: the ecosystem, the package each one calls it, and the version that fixes it there. A component vendored into many products fans out widely here, which is the point: it is why a single CVE can need a dozen separate upgrades. These are the feed's fix versions, not a patch plan for this fleet. Nothing here knows which of these you run or at what version. Matching hosts in this fleet above is the panel that does. Version nodes carry their package and distribution, because two packages fixing at "1.2.3" are not one node and merging them would draw a route that does not exist. Crowded columns collapse into a single node rather than becoming unreadable.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_ranges_lookup where cve_id="$cve_tok$" | eval Introduced = if(introduced="", "any earlier version", introduced) | eval Fixed = case(fixed != "", fixed, last_affected != "", "no fix; last affected " . last_affected, 1=1, "no fix published") | eval Distribution = trim(distro . " " . distro_release) | stats values(Fixed) AS Fixed, values(Introduced) AS Introduced BY ecosystem, package, Distribution | rename ecosystem AS Ecosystem, package AS Package | sort 0 Ecosystem, Package, Distribution

viz.option: No affected ranges for this CVE in the bundle.

div.span: One CVE usually has several advisories: the upstream one, and one per distribution that shipped a fix. They disagree about version numbers on purpose, because each describes its own packaging.
